articles.title: Review: All Basic Tenses
articles.desc: Revisao dos tempos verbais basicos em ingles: Simple Present, Simple Past, Simple Future, Present/Past Continuous.
articles.essential: Simple Present: rotinas (I study). Simple Past: acoes concluidas (I studied). Simple Future: will + verbo (I will study), going to (planos). Present Continuous: agora (I am studying). Past Continuous: acao em andamento no passado (I was studying). Auxiliares: do/does, did, will.
articles.body:
Introducao

Os tempos verbais basicos sao a fundacao do ingles.

Tempos

TempoUsoExemplo
Simple PresentRotinas, fatosShe studies every day
Simple PastAcoes concluidasShe studied yesterday
Simple FuturePrevisoes, decisoesShe will study tomorrow
Present ContinuousAgoraShe is studying now
Past ContinuousEm andamento no passadoShe was studying

Resumo

  • Present: rotina. Past: concluido. Future: will/going to.
  • ENEM: tempos verbais em contexto de leitura

Curiosidade

O ingles tem 12 tempos verbais, mas no dia a dia usamos cerca de 5-6 com frequencia!

faq.a: Rotinas (I wake up at 7), fatos (Water boils at 100C), horarios fixos (The train leaves at 9).
Will: decisoes espontaneas, previsoes. Going to: planos ja decididos. 'I will help you' (agora decidi) vs 'I'm going to travel' (ja planejei).
Past Continuous: acao EM ANDAMENTO quando outra aconteceu. 'I was sleeping WHEN the phone rang.' Sleeping=cont, rang=simple.
Do/does (present), did (past), will (future). Usados em perguntas e negativas. 'Do you study?' 'She doesn't work.' 'Did they go?'

articles.title: Present Perfect: Experience and Result
articles.desc: Present Perfect: have/has + past participle. Experiencias, resultados, acoes com relevancia no presente. Ever, never, already, yet, since, for.
articles.essential: Present Perfect: have/has + past participle. Usos: experiencias (I have visited Paris), resultado presente (She has lost her keys), acoes inacabadas (I have lived here since 2020). Marcadores: ever (ja, em perguntas), never (nunca), already (ja), yet (ainda nao), since (desde ponto), for (durante periodo). Diferenca: Simple Past = quando. Present Perfect = experiencia/resultado.
articles.body:
Introducao

O Present Perfect conecta passado ao presente.

Formacao

have/has + past participle (3a coluna)

Usos

UsoExemplo
ExperienciaI have visited Japan
ResultadoShe has broken her arm
Desde/duranteI have lived here since 2020

Since vs For

  • Since: ponto no tempo (since 2020, since Monday)
  • For: periodo de tempo (for 3 years, for 2 hours)

Resumo

  • Have/has + participio. Passado com efeito no presente.
  • ENEM: interpretacao de textos com present perfect

Curiosidade

Em portugues NAO temos Present Perfect exato! 'I have lived here for 5 years' = 'Moro aqui ha 5 anos' (presente em PT!).

faq.a: Simple Past: acao acabou, QUANDO importa (I visited Paris in 2019). Present Perfect: experiencia, QUANDO nao importa (I have visited Paris).
Since: ponto (since January, since 2020). For: duracao (for 3 months, for 10 years). Since + data. For + periodo.
Ever: 'alguma vez' (Have you EVER been to London?). Never: 'nunca' (I have NEVER eaten sushi). Usados com experiencias.
Already: 'ja' em afirmativas (I have already finished). Yet: 'ainda' em negativas/perguntas (I haven't finished yet / Have you finished yet?).

articles.title: Modal Verbs: Ability, Permission, Obligation
articles.desc: Modal verbs: can/could (habilidade), may/might (possibilidade), must/have to (obrigacao), should (conselho), would (hipotese).
articles.essential: Can: habilidade (I can swim), permissao informal (Can I go?). Could: habilidade passada, pedido educado. May: permissao formal, possibilidade (It may rain). Might: possibilidade menor. Must: obrigacao forte, deducao (She must be tired). Have to: obrigacao externa. Should: conselho (You should study). Would: hipotese, educacao (Would you like...?). Must not: proibicao. Don't have to: nao precisa.
articles.body:
Introducao

Os modal verbs modificam o sentido do verbo principal.

Modais

ModalUsoExemplo
CanHabilidade/permissaoI can swim
MustObrigacao/deducaoYou must study
ShouldConselhoYou should rest
May/MightPossibilidadeIt may rain
WouldHipotese/educacaoWould you like tea?

Must not vs Don't have to

  • Must not: PROIBIDO (You must not cheat)
  • Don't have to: nao precisa (You don't have to come)

Resumo

  • Modais nao conjugam (sem s, ed, ing)
  • ENEM: modais em textos, interpretacao

Curiosidade

'Can' e 'may' confundem brasileiros: can=informal, may=formal. Professor diz: 'You CAN go, but you MAY NOT.'

faq.a: Must: obrigacao interna ('Eu devo'). Have to: obrigacao externa ('Preciso porque a regra exige'). Na pratica, muito parecidos.
Should: conselho ('Voce deveria'). Must: obrigacao ('Voce deve'). Should e mais suave.
Ambos indicam possibilidade. May: mais provavel. Might: menos provavel. 'It may rain' (provavel) vs 'It might rain' (menos certo).
NAO! Can, must, should, may nunca levam s, ed ou ing. Nao usam auxiliar (do/does). 'She can swim' (nao 'she cans').

articles.title: Passive Voice
articles.desc: Voz passiva em ingles: formacao (be + past participle). Usos: foco no objeto, agente desconhecido. Passiva em todos os tempos.
articles.essential: Voz ativa: sujeito faz acao (The cat ate the fish). Voz passiva: sujeito recebe acao (The fish was eaten by the cat). Formacao: be + past participle. By + agente (opcional). Usos: quando o OBJETO e mais importante, agente desconhecido, textos cientificos, jornalisticos. Tempos: is/are + pp (present), was/were + pp (past), will be + pp (future), has been + pp (present perfect).
articles.body:
Introducao

A voz passiva coloca o foco em quem RECEBE a acao.

Formacao

Sujeito + be + past participle (+ by agente)

Exemplos

AtivaPassiva
They build housesHouses are built (by them)
She wrote a bookA book was written (by her)
They will fix itIt will be fixed

Resumo

  • Be + past participle. Foco no objeto.
  • ENEM: passiva em textos jornalisticos e cientificos

Curiosidade

Textos cientificos usam MUITO passiva: 'The experiment was conducted...' - o foco e no experimento, nao em quem fez!

faq.a: Quando o agente e desconhecido (My car was stolen), quando o objeto importa mais (The Mona Lisa was painted by Da Vinci), textos formais.
Nao! So use 'by + agente' se o agente for RELEVANTE. 'The window was broken' (nao importa por quem). 'America was discovered by Columbus' (importa).
Has/have been + past participle. 'The email has been sent.' 'The books have been delivered.'
Sim, tende a ser mais formal. Textos academicos, jornalisticos, cientificos preferem passiva. Conversas informais preferem ativa.

articles.title: Conditional Sentences (If Clauses)
articles.desc: Condicionais: Zero (fatos), First (possivel), Second (hipotetico), Third (impossivel/arrependimento). If-clauses.
articles.essential: Zero conditional: If + present, present (fatos: If you heat water, it boils). First: If + present, will + verbo (possivel: If it rains, I will stay home). Second: If + past, would + verbo (hipotetico: If I had money, I would travel). Third: If + past perfect, would have + pp (impossivel: If I had studied, I would have passed). Mixed conditionals existem mas sao raras no ENEM.
articles.body:
Introducao

As conditional sentences expressam condicao e consequencia.

Tipos

TipoEstruturaUso
ZeroIf + present, presentFatos
FirstIf + present, willPossivel
SecondIf + past, wouldHipotetico
ThirdIf + past perfect, would have + ppImpossivel

Resumo

  • Zero=fato. First=possivel. Second=hipotese. Third=impossivel.
  • ENEM: interpretar condicionais em textos

Curiosidade

Na Second Conditional, usamos 'were' para TODAS as pessoas: 'If I WERE you...' (nao 'If I was')!

faq.q: If I were vs If I was?
faq.a: Formalmente: 'If I WERE' (subjuntivo). Informalmente: 'If I was' e aceito. No ENEM, espere 'were'.
First: possivel/provavel (If it rains...). Second: improvavel/hipotetico (If I won the lottery...). Diferenca de probabilidade.
Falar de passado impossivel de mudar. Arrependimento: 'If I had studied harder, I would have passed.' Nao estudei, nao passei. Tarde demais.
Sim! 'If it rains, I'll stay' = 'I'll stay if it rains'. Mesma coisa. Virgula quando if vem primeiro.

quiz.question: If it rains, I ___ stay home
If I ___ rich, I would travel
If I had studied, I ___ passed

articles.title: Relative Clauses
articles.desc: Relative clauses: who (pessoas), which (coisas), that (ambos), where (lugar), whose (posse). Defining vs non-defining.
articles.essential: Relative clauses: oracoes que descrevem/identificam um substantivo. Who: pessoas. Which: coisas/animais. That: ambos (informal). Where: lugar. Whose: posse. Defining: essencial para o sentido (sem virgula). Non-defining: informacao extra (COM virgula). 'The man WHO called...' (defining). 'My mom, WHO is a doctor, ...' (non-defining).
articles.body:
Introducao

As relative clauses adicionam informacao sobre um substantivo.

Pronomes

PronomeUsoExemplo
whoPessoasThe girl who studies
whichCoisasThe book which I read
thatAmbosThe dog that barks
whereLugarThe city where I live
whosePosseThe boy whose mom called

Resumo

  • Who=pessoa, which=coisa, that=ambos
  • ENEM: interpretar relative clauses em textos

Curiosidade

No ingles informal, 'that' substitui 'who' e 'which' quase sempre! Na escrita formal, use o correto.

faq.a: Defining: essencial. 'The man who called me is my boss.' (QUAL homem?). Non-defining: extra. 'My boss, who is tall, called me.' (ja sabemos quem e).
Sim, quando ele e OBJETO. 'The book (which) I read.' Nao quando e SUJEITO: 'The man who called' (nao pode tirar).
Where = in which. 'The city where I live' = 'The city in which I live'. Where e mais simples.
Indica POSSE. 'The student whose grade was highest...' = 'O aluno cuja nota...' Funciona com pessoas e coisas.

quiz.question: The boy ___ mom is a doctor

articles.title: Reported Speech (Indirect Speech)
articles.desc: Reported speech: transformar fala direta em indireta. Mudancas de tempo verbal, pronomes, referencias de tempo/lugar.
articles.essential: Direct: 'I am happy,' she said. Reported: She said (that) she was happy. Mudancas: am/is→was, are→were, will→would, can→could, present→past. Pronomes mudam conforme o contexto. Tempo: today→that day, yesterday→the day before, tomorrow→the next day. Here→there. Reporting verbs: said, told, asked, explained.
articles.body:
Introducao

O reported speech transforma fala direta em indireta.

Mudancas

DirectReported
am/iswas
arewere
willwould
cancould
todaythat day
herethere

Exemplo

  • Direct: 'I will come tomorrow.'
  • Reported: He said he would come the next day.

Resumo

  • Verbos recuam 1 tempo. Pronomes mudam.
  • ENEM: interpretar reported speech em textos

Curiosidade

Em ingles, o 'that' do reported speech e OPCIONAL! 'She said (that) she was tired.'

faq.a: Quando o reporting verb esta no passado (said, told), sim. Se esta no presente (says, tells), nao precisa mudar.
Said: sem complemento ('She said...'). Told: com complemento ('She told ME...'). Never: 'She said me' (ERRADO!).
Mudam para ordem afirmativa. 'Where do you live?' → He asked where I lived. Sem ponto de interrogacao!
'Study hard!' → She told me TO STUDY hard. 'Don't go!' → He told me NOT TO GO. Usar to + infinitive.

quiz.question: 'I am tired' → She said she ___ tired

articles.title: Reading Strategies: Genres and Comprehension
articles.desc: Estrategias de leitura: skimming, scanning, inferencia. Generos textuais: artigo, email, anuncio, cartoon, poema, musica.
articles.essential: Skimming: leitura rapida para ideia geral. Scanning: buscar informacao especifica. Inferencia: deduzir significado pelo contexto. Cognatos: palavras parecidas com portugues (information=informacao). Falsos cognatos: actually=na verdade (nao 'atualmente'). Generos no ENEM: artigos, anuncios, emails, cartuns, letras de musica, poemas, noticias, tirinhas.
articles.body:
Introducao

A leitura estrategica e a chave para interpretar textos em ingles no ENEM.

Estrategias

EstrategiaO que faz
SkimmingLeitura rapida, ideia geral
ScanningBuscar dado especifico
InferenciaDeduzir pelo contexto
CognatosPalavras parecidas com PT

Generos

  • Artigo, email, noticia, anuncio, cartoon, tirinha, poema, musica

Resumo

  • Nao precisa traduzir tudo! Use estrategias.
  • ENEM testa COMPREENSAO, nao traducao

Curiosidade

Cerca de 30% das palavras em ingles tem origem latina - por isso tantos cognatos com o portugues!

faq.a: NAO! ENEM testa compreensao, nao traducao palavra por palavra. Use cognatos, contexto, imagens. Nao entre em panico com palavras desconhecidas.
Skimming: passar os olhos para ter IDEIA GERAL. Scanning: buscar INFO ESPECIFICA (numero, nome, data). Ambos sao leitura rapida.
MUITO! Information=informacao, important=importante, culture=cultura. ~30% das palavras em ingles sao cognatas. Mas cuidado com falsos cognatos!
Actually=na verdade. Pretend=fingir. Push=empurrar. Resume=retomar. Library=biblioteca. Sensitive=sensivel.
